title: Recording: Mama’s Little Girl, Big Barn Bed by Wings | 1972
content:
Studio Two, EMI Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Alan Parsons

Wings worked on two songs on 17 November 1972: ‘Mama’s Little Girl’ and ‘Big Barn Bed’.

Both songs were destined for different fates. ‘Big Barn Bed’ became the opening track on the Red Rose Speedway album, but ‘Mama’s Little Girl’ remained unreleased until Paul McCartney’s ‘Put It There’ single in 1990.

It was decided that ‘Mama’s Little Girl’ required a clarinet overdub, and EMI’s Vera Samwell arranged a handful of players to attend this session. McCartney did not prepare a score, but played the parts he wanted on a piano, which the players transcribed. The overdub was completed in just one take.

The rest of the session was taken up with ‘Big Barn Bed’. Denny Seiwell re-recorded the drum track, and backing vocals and percussion were also overdubbed.
